# @displayxr/inline3d — DisplayXR inline-3D web SDK

> Glasses-free 3D for web pages on a DisplayXR spatial display: you render one image per eye into a
> canvas, the DisplayXR Browser weaves them for the panel; an ordinary browser shows the page in 2D.

Read first: docs/making-3d-look-right.md — the rules: rig choice, keep the object-viewer defaults,
fixed convergence for worlds, dark grey not black, 2D UI and cover rules, depth slider, 2D/3D switch.

## Start from a sample
- samples/model/ — product / object viewer (glTF) with addModel
- samples/hello-cube/ — your own three.js loop on a display rig (EyeCamera)
- samples/camera-rig/ — a camera rig (cameraRigFromCamera, the attach pattern)
- samples/display-modes/ — 2D/3D switch with setStereoEnabled
- samples/splat/ — Gaussian splat with addSplat

## Reference
- docs/authoring-inline-3d.md — every API, both view rigs, comfort maths
- docs/woven-canvas-rules.md — what the browser does to a woven canvas; CSS, remount and cover rules
- docs/porting-three-js-apps.md — moving an existing three.js app over
- docs/authoring-motion-and-effects.md, docs/splat-effects.md — motion, reveals, depth envelopes
- index.d.ts, three.d.ts, viewer.d.ts, model.d.ts, splat.d.ts — the public API with JSDoc
- CHANGELOG.md — what changed per release
